steps.message: The project lives inside a gitignored directory of an outer repo, so `git diff` is empty. Here are the changes:

## Diagnosis

The root cause was in `Preferences.java`'s `chkDarkTheme` `OnPreferenceChangeListener`:

```java
finish();
final Intent intent = getIntent();
intent.setFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK | Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
startActivity(intent);
```

`FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK` wipes the entire task before relaunching `Preferences`. That was deliberate (it's the only way the old code could get the already-created `GpsTestActivity` to re-read the theme preference), but it destroys `GpsTestActivity`, so pressing back exits the app instead of returning to the main screen — exactly the observed behavior.

## Fix

Took the "apply the theme to `GpsTestActivity` and still allow the user to return to it" option from the report, rather than just adding a warning message:

**`Preferences.java`** — the theme change now only re-creates the Settings screen itself, leaving the back stack intact. The `recreate()` is posted to the main looper so the `CheckBoxPreference` persists the new value before `onCreate()` re-reads it (returning `true` from the listener is what triggers the write, so recreating synchronously would race it). Added `android.os.Handler` / `android.os.Looper` imports.

**`GpsTestActivity.java`** — added a `mUseDarkTheme` field recording which theme was actually applied in `onCreate()`, and a check at the end of `onResume()` that calls `recreate()` when the stored value no longer matches the preference. Since `onCreate()` always syncs the field to the current preference, the re-created instance's check passes and there's no recreate loop. The check is placed *after* the listener registration in `onResume()` so `onPause()`'s teardown stays balanced during the destroy/recreate cycle. This also refreshes `NavigationDrawerFragment`, which applies its dark-theme colors programmatically at view-creation time.

Net behavior: toggling "Use Dark Theme" re-themes the Settings screen immediately, and pressing back returns to `GpsTestActivity`, which re-themes itself as it resumes.

## Diagnosis

The root cause was in `Preferences.java`'s `chkDarkTheme` `OnPreferenceChangeListener`:

```java
finish();
final Intent intent = getIntent();
intent.setFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK | Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
startActivity(intent);
```

`FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK` wipes the entire task before relaunching `Preferences`. That was deliberate (it's the only way the old code could get the already-created `GpsTestActivity` to re-read the theme preference), but it destroys `GpsTestActivity`, so pressing back exits the app instead of returning to the main screen — exactly the observed behavior.

## Fix

Took the "apply the theme to `GpsTestActivity` and still allow the user to return to it" option from the report, rather than just adding a warning message:

**`Preferences.java`** — the theme change now only re-creates the Settings screen itself, leaving the back stack intact. The `recreate()` is posted to the main looper so the `CheckBoxPreference` persists the new value before `onCreate()` re-reads it (returning `true` from the listener is what triggers the write, so recreating synchronously would race it). Added `android.os.Handler` / `android.os.Looper` imports.

**`GpsTestActivity.java`** — added a `mUseDarkTheme` field recording which theme was actually applied in `onCreate()`, and a check at the end of `onResume()` that calls `recreate()` when the stored value no longer matches the preference. Since `onCreate()` always syncs the field to the current preference, the re-created instance's check passes and there's no recreate loop. The check is placed *after* the listener registration in `onResume()` so `onPause()`'s teardown stays balanced during the destroy/recreate cycle. This also refreshes `NavigationDrawerFragment`, which applies its dark-theme colors programmatically at view-creation time.

Net behavior: toggling "Use Dark Theme" re-themes the Settings screen immediately, and pressing back returns to `GpsTestActivity`, which re-themes itself as it resumes.

`./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**.
